answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (report.py output):

RECORDS & ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20; window 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, covering 3.314% of the time span)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 of them above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc)

INJECTION / EXTRACTION (15.96 days)
- Injected: 4.654e+05 m3; extracted: 5.059e+05 m3; net -4.048e+04 m3 (net extraction)

CATALOGUE (LBNL/NCEDC March 2016, GDR 859)
- 5 events, ML from -0.48 to 0.07

CALIBRATED PROBABILITIES (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated estimate, using the LBNL catalogue):
  b      Sigma      P(Mw>=5.5)/yr   P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume   P(Mw>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198       5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922        0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474         0.0006484                        0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at/above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is an upper bound, NOT calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is at most ~1.5e-2/yr (b=0.65) and as low as ~1.2e-4/yr (b=1.0), i.e. very low. The DAS-based number (0.078/yr) is an upper bound that over-counts because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are treated as events at/above Mc; the calibrated LBNL-catalogue values are the ones to trust.
